title: Nobody has tested a restore or a rollback, and point-in-time recovery fails today
summary: The binlog upload stopped on 9 October, and the rollback path does not exist. Fix the upload now, then build the rollback path and rehearse it two times before the cutover.

badges.tip: The cutover date depends on two passed rollback rehearsals.
Step 1 needs no decision. Each day without it adds risk.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: A backup has value only if a restore works. A cutover is safe only if a rollback works. Nobody has tested either one.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [READ] The run book has no record of a restore test. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] I restored last night's snapshot to a scratch instance. The restore took 6 h 12 min. The row counts match on all 46 tables. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] Point-in-time recovery failed. The binlog upload job stopped on 9 October 2026, after a credential change. [src: report.md]
  • [READ] The reverse replication from PostgreSQL to MySQL does not exist yet. [src: report.md]
  • [UNVERIFIED] The rollback time of about 20 minutes is an estimate. Nobody has rehearsed it.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html:
• Today, a failure loses up to 24 hours of orders. [INFERRED]
  • After the cutover, a failure without a rollback path loses every order since the switch. [INFERRED]

blocks.title: Proposed action
blocks.html:
1. Fix the binlog upload now. Add an alert for the case that no file arrives in 1 hour.
  2. Repeat the restore test, with point-in-time recovery.
  3. Build the reverse replication.
  4. Rehearse a full rollback in staging two times.
  5. Make two passed rehearsals a go/no-go gate (D5).

Effort: 6.5 days.
